Same grade as peer NLY (3/10).

description.text: AGNC Investment Corp. ("AGNC," the "Company," "we," "us" and "our") was organized on January 7, 2008 and commenced operations on May 20, 2008 following the completion of our initial public offering. Our common stock is traded on The Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "AGNC." We are a leading provider of private capital to the U.S. housing market, enhancing liquidity in the residential real estate mortgage markets and, in turn, facilitating home ownership in the U.S. We invest primarily in Agency residential mortgage-backed securities ("Agency RMBS") on a leveraged basis. These investments consist of residential mortgage pass-through securities and collateralized mortgage obligations for which the principal and interest payments are guaranteed by a U.S. Government-sponsored enterprise, such as the Federal National Mortgage Association ("Fannie Mae") and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation ("Freddie Mac," and together with Fannie Mae, the "GSEs"), or by a U.S. Government agency, such as the Government National Mortgage Association ("Ginnie Mae"). We operate to qualify to be taxed as a real estate investment trust ("REIT") under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Internal Revenue Code"). As a REIT, we are required to distribute annually 90% of our taxable income, and we will generally not be subject to U.S. federal or state corporate income tax to the extent that we distribute all our annual taxable income to our stockholders on a timely basis.

about.description_short: Founded in 2008, AGNC Investment Corp. (Nasdaq: AGNC) is a leading investor in Agency residential mortgage-backed securities (Agency MBS), which benefit from a guarantee against credit losses by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, or Ginnie Mae. We invest on a leveraged basis, financing our Agency MBS assets primarily through repurchase agreements, and utilize dynamic risk management strategies intended to protect the value of our portfolio from interest rate and other market risks. AGNC has a track record of providing favorable long-term returns for our stockholders through substantial monthly dividend income, with over $16 billion of common stock dividends paid since inception. Our business is a significant source of private capital for the U.S. residential housing market, and our team has extensive experience managing mortgage assets across market cycles.

analysis_md:
# AGNC — AGNC Investment Corp.
Engine 5.5 run, 2026-10-19. In scope (market cap $8.640B at $8.44, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or statements.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Bethesda, Maryland Agency mortgage REIT (internally managed, operating since 2008): it holds a leveraged portfolio of residential mortgage pass-through securities and CMOs guaranteed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae — $97.2B investment portfolio at Q2 2026, 94% in 30-year fixed-rate Agency MBS and TBA securities (company reporting) — funded mainly with repurchase agreements at ~7.4x tangible-equity leverage (Q2 2026, company reporting). The product is a levered interest-rate spread: asset yield minus repo funding cost, hedged with swaps/TBAs. It pays a $0.12 monthly dividend ($1.44/yr, unchanged since 2020) and grows the portfolio by issuing shares through an at-the-market program.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $653M; SBC $26M (always a real cost); capex $0 — by filing override, see OVERRIDE.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $627M = $0.61/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share $0.6125 in dcf_numbers.json).
- The maintenance definition is not computable for this filer: no depreciation/amortization tag is filed (da is blank in every year of financials_history.csv), so the CSV leaves oe_maintenance blank. The conservative OCF-based figure is the only engine definition available — one more reason this is a low-confidence, sector-misfit read.
- OE positive 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (FY2023 was negative: OE/share -$0.21).
- Balance sheet (FY2025, statements.json): total assets $115,077M, total liabilities $102,684M, equity $12,393M; cash $450M and restricted cash $1,292M (financials_history.csv). The liabilities are overwhelmingly the repo/secured borrowings that fund the MBS book — see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK under Flags. ## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification: a commodity spread vehicle whose only durable advantages are scale ($97.2B portfolio), deep repo/TBA market access, internal management and accretive ATM issuance when the shares trade above tangible book — the assets are government-guaranteed securities anyone with financing can buy, spreads and funding costs are market-set, and there is no pricing power or switching cost.
- Evidence first (fundamentals.json): the `roic_proxy` series is null for every year (no operating-income tag is filed) and gross margin is not a meaningful metric for a spread lender, so the return evidence is ROE, which swung from -15.1% (FY2022) to +1.9% (FY2023), +8.8% (FY2024) and +13.5% (FY2025) — rate/spread-driven, not franchise-driven, and book value per share fell over the same era (fundamentals.json BVPS $20.09 in FY2020 → $12.11 in FY2025; tangible book $8.58 at Q2 2026, company reporting, is +9.9% YoY but well below its level of five years ago). A 7+ moat cannot sit on that record; this matches peer NLY's 3/10.
- FOR: one of the two largest Agency mREITs ($97.2B investment portfolio at Q2 2026) with deep, preferred access to repo funding and the TBA/dollar-roll market; internally managed — no external-manager fee drag — with an operating history since 2008 through multiple rate cycles; demonstrated accretive capital raising (Q2 2026 ATM issuance of $167M at ~$10.31/share against $8.58 tangible book, company reporting); pure Agency book (94% 30-year fixed Agency MBS/TBA) — no credit/default risk in the assets.
- AGAINST: no pricing power — Agency MBS spreads and repo costs are market-set and the product is a commodity financial asset; structural leverage (~7.4x tangible equity) makes book value hostage to rate and spread moves; persistent equity dilution — diluted share count growing 24.0%/yr (engine DILUTION flag), 530.0M shares in FY2021 to 1,023.7M in FY2025 and 1,185,481,447 shares outstanding at 2026-07-30 (dcf_numbers.json), so per-share spread income barely grows even when the portfolio does; ROE is cyclical and sign-flipping with no demonstrated through-cycle return above the cost of equity; the $1.44/yr dividend has been held flat since 2020 while book value per share eroded.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 5.9 years, 15-year projection.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:capex / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: see OVERRIDE — gap, decision and measured impact (nil on OE; binary unblock) are recorded in judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json, score.json and the registry.
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended ~10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $0.61 vs 3-yr median $0.09): the median is the distorted one. FY2023–FY2024 are the rate-shock trough: repo funding repriced years before the legacy low-coupon portfolio could (interest expense $625M in FY2022 → $2,287M in FY2023 → $2,931M in FY2024, statements.json) while interest income lagged ($1,590M FY2022 → $2,041M FY2023), driving GAAP net interest income to -$246M in FY2023 and $18M in FY2024. By FY2025 the book had repriced (interest income $3,523M; net interest income $675M; portfolio weighted-average coupon 5.04% at Q2 2026, company reporting). The TTM base ($0.75) sits on the repriced book; the median ($0.09) averages in a funding regime that no longer exists.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (NI vs OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): two structural mechanisms, no error in either series. (1) Net income carries non-cash mark-to-market on the MBS book and hedges — other non-operating income of +$497M (FY2023), +$955M (FY2024) and +$1,122M (FY2025) in statements.json — which operating cash flow reverses out; that is why FY2025 net income of $1,670M prints against OCF of $653M, and why TTM net income is $2,266M against TTM OCF of $886M (fundamentals.json). (2) OCF tracks the cash spread, which troughed with the repricing lag described under BASE_DIVERGENCE (OCF -$118M in FY2023). Resolution: the OCF-based conservative OE is the series used throughout, and the divergence is the reason the base is read as a floor against the company's spread-income measure (see Owner's earnings).
- **DILUTION** (share count +24.0%/yr): real and structural — it is the funding model, not compensation creep (TTM SBC is $24M, ~2.7% of TTM OCF). Diluted shares went from 530,000,000 (FY2021) to 1,023,700,000 (FY2025), with 1,185,481,447 outstanding at 2026-07-30 (dcf_numbers.json). Issuance at a premium to tangible book is per-share accretive; issuance near or below book is not. The growth starts were set per-share with this drag in front of them (base +3% against a portfolio growing double-digits). No mechanical dilution adjustment entered the forecast: every growth component in dcf_numbers.json is null (no revenue series for an mREIT), so the blend fell back to the neutral 3.00% and the engine's -5pp share adjustment had no component to deduct from — dilution is carried qualitatively instead, in the per-share growth starts, the bear-heavy probabilities (45% bear-or-worse) and the bear-end sizing.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range spans >3x over 5 years): real — OE/share ran -$0.21 / $0.09 / $0.61 over FY2023–25 and $1.88–$3.13 in FY2020–22 on a much smaller share count. Handled by the TTM base (post-repricing window) and bear-heavy probabilities (45% on bear-or-worse).
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (no diluted count filed for 2014): history-only — 2014 is outside the base window and the TTM; per-share figures for that year are approximate and nothing in the verdict rests on them.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag for the latest FY — net debt UNKNOWN, not zero): stated from the filing instead (FY2025 10-K balance sheet, verified by direct read): total liabilities $102,684M against total assets $115,077M and equity $12,393M, of which the single dominant line is **repurchase agreements $85,286M** (plus an obligation to return securities borrowed under reverse repurchase agreements of $16,452M); cash $450M plus restricted cash $1,292M (financials_history.csv). The engine reads no debt tag because an mREIT's borrowings are repurchase agreements/secured financings against the securities book, not the corporate debt tags the engine reads. Leverage verdict: this is a levered carry vehicle by design — company-reported leverage was 7.4x tangible equity at Q2 2026 — so "net debt" in the corporate sense is the whole balance sheet; the DCF's net-debt diagnostic is not applicable and is recorded as null, not zero.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range. On the filing-direct OCF definition this is a C by numbers (11.83% weighted IRR) that only clears 15% below ~$6.28. On the company's own spread economics (net spread and dollar roll income ~$0.40/share/quarter at Q2 2026, dividend covered 1.11x, tangible book compounding +9.9% YoY), the same company looks materially cheaper — the same ~2x base gap NLY showed against its EAD. Both reads agree on the thing that matters most: at $8.44, essentially tangible book value, the market is not paying for spread widening; it is paying for the current ~2% spread to persist.
- What the buyer actually owns: a monthly $0.12 dividend ($1.44/yr, a ~17% yield on $8.44) funded by a levered Agency book, with book value that compounds when spreads widen or rates fall and erodes when the opposite happens (BVPS $20.09 in FY2020 → $12.11 in FY2025 on the total-equity basis is the long-run warning; the last four quarters are the recovery).
- The dilution machine cuts both ways and is the swing factor for per-share outcomes: +24%/yr share growth at premiums to book builds tangible book per share (Q2 2026 issuance at ~$10.31 vs $8.58 book); the same machine issuing near book in a selloff would lock in the bear case. The scenario weights put 45% on bear-or-worse for exactly this reflexivity.
- Margin of safety on the final numbers: the weighted IV@15% ($6.28) sits 25.6% below the price and even the bull IV@15% ($8.22) sits below it — on this model's inputs a buyer at $8.44 is paid only in the super-bull path (19.57% IRR, 10% weight). The offsetting fact, stated once more because it is the whole debate: this model's base demonstrably understates the company's spread earnings measure by ~2x, so the DCF verdict is a conservative floor, not a fair-value estimate.
